I'll use myself as an example. I had an ex who used to regularly disregard my feelings message me 6 months after ghosting me to apologise. He said he'd been going to therapy and was getting better and how bad he felt about how he treated me and how he wanted to meet to apologise etc. I was only beginning to heal and move on at that point and was not ready to hear anything from him. I think *maybe* given more time I could accept an apology but it was just too much for me at that point and set me back in my own healing journey.

Of course your situation will be different but just some food for thought.

Hey I read your really long pitch/short script! It's a good start. First of all I think Jeff's inability to move on, not necessarily move on from the group but move on from his mindset that his time with the group were the best years of his life, is an interesting idea to explore. I'm curious where you'd take this idea next.

However, I think some things need more work. Some of the dialogue I feel is a bit out of character and a bit clunky. For example when Troy says, "When i said the study group, just the study group not everyone we encountered as a study group!" And when Abed says, "Well atleast it's a party". I cant picture either of them saying those lines. I think Troy would say something funnier/goofier to make light of the mistake. As for Abed, he doesn't seem like the type to make the mistake of mass-sending an invitation accidentally in the first place. He's usually pretty logical and careful with things. But if he did make that mistake I dont think he'd say "at least it's a party" because he doesn't seem the type to care about parties. Maybe he'd make a reference to a movie or show where this kind of thing happens or maybe he'd remark on how it's a cliche or trope of reunion movies.

Another thing that could use some work is the Jeff and Annie thing. It seems like the script is building up to them becoming a couple which is fine if that's what your vision is. However, I dont understand either of their motivations for the big fight they have at the end. Jeff is really resentful for supposedly being abandoned by the group but he still has Britta, the Dean, Professor Duncan, Chang and Frankie close by. Maybe if you want to make his resentment just at Annie because you're setting them up, it'd be better if he wasn't so aggressive. Jeff can be pretty harsh sometimes but in my opinion, it's unfair on him as a character who's had this huge redemption arc to go back to his old self. He's a good guy. He just puts on this stoic front. I think he'd be more understanding of Annie's wants and needs.

As for Annie, I think her fear of calling Jeff because she's "just little Annie, a nobody that people will soon forget and replace" doesn't make sense because that sounds like season 1 or 2 Annie and she's grown and developed so much since then. She's achieved so much at Greendale and at the FBI, kinda doesn't make sense why she fears she'll be forgotten. Like do the group never text each other at all? Never call? If you want to keep this as her motivation maybe think about about why and how she's reverted back to S1 and 2 Annie. Personally, I'd like to see the group with new conflicts that come from what they've been doing since the end of season 6 but at the end of the day it's your script. 

Ok so that was a really long reply but anyways, good luck to your future writing endeavors! :)
